clauses.reason: Terminated by own terms: 'until July 31, 1934' (stated date inclusive, 1934-07-31; exclusive reading one day earlier). Actor EO:6577 itself. Later events: new 'further exemption' grants of the same person, each with its own date and quote; none revokes or amends this order.

research_rationale:
EO:6577 (1934-01-25) is a single-clause order under section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 exempting Carleton W. Sturtevant, principal engineer, Engineer Department at Large, War Department from compulsory retirement for age and continuing the person in the service 'until July 31, 1934'. The order ends by its own terms on 1934-07-31 (stated date, inclusive; exclusive alternative one day earlier, per the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling on 'until' dates). Later orders in the same person's exemption chain, read in the packet: EO:6773 (1934-06-30); EO:7217 (1935-10-30); each is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote (owner ruling, 2026-10-21), and none revokes, amends or shortens this order. Six-month exemption; its text states no birthday. The 'twenty-one months' recited in EO 7217 is the sum of this order's term and EO 6773's (January 25, 1934 to November 1, 1935), consistent with the stated until-dates. The dossier's machine term leads were read against the text; the operative until-date in the command sentence is the end. @rationale:retirement:statute @rationale:retirement:search @rationale:retirement:inventory

A later 'further' exemption of the same person is a new grant under the statute, not a savings clause of this order, and the person's employment after the stated date rests on that later order, not on this one.
